data.narrative:
Sphere Semi is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $20M to date. The founding team brings relevant domain expertise: CEO Steven Glinert is a repeat founder with economics training, while CTO Mitchell Nahmias holds a PhD in photonic integrated circuits and co-founded Luminous Computing. The broader Chips & Semiconductors sector encompasses 11 private peers (including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched) and three public comparables (NVDA, AMD, ALAB), though no peers are sufficiently comparable at Sphere's stage and valuation tier to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Given the scarcity of narrow-set peers, the Stage-Progression method provides the primary valuation anchor. Applying a typical 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage multiplier to the $20M raised proxy yields an implied valuation of $50M. This reflects standard step-up dynamics between Seed and Series A financing rounds in frontier semiconductor hardware.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $42M to $57M, with a median of $50M. Key uncertainties center on technology differentiation and market timing within photonic computing—a subsector where public and private comparables trade on highly disparate multiple regimes. The thin peer set limits confidence in multiple-based approaches; investors should weight prototype maturity, IP defensibility, and commercial traction as key due-diligence levers before committing capital.
